thread:
SRE-Bot: [ALERT] sfo1 edge-gateway cluster: all control-plane endpoints UNREACHABLE, health checks failing, severity=P1 :rotating_light:
Evan: oncall here, seeing 100% 5xx from sfo1 LB in dashboards. customers hitting errors.
Priya: control-plane heartbeats for sfo1 are missing since 02:04 UTC — prometheus shows no kube-apiserver metrics.
Jorge: trying to SSH one of the edge gateways -> `ssh: connect to host 10.8.3.7 port 22: Connection timed out`
Marta: @here what's the blast radius? Dedicated pools in sfo1 (redwood-dedicated-gpu-pool-a) serving ~12% of traffic. Hosted API routes also have nodes in sfo1.
Evan: early ask: do we have automated region failover enabled for global LB? it doesn't look like it flipped yet.
Oncall-Leads: paging infra escalation now — paging list oncall+infra-leads, tagging cloud-networking team.
Support-Shift: starting customer comms draft, will mark affected customers with sfo1 capacity.
Priya: running quick probes: `curl -sS -D - https://edge.sfo1.redwood-internal/health`
Priya: ```
HTTP/1.1 524 A Timeout Occurred
Server: nginx
X-Req-Id: abc123
```
Jorge: digging into provider console, control-plane VPC appears reachable to provider but BGP sessions show flap events around 02:03 UTC.
Marta: could be provider backbone or regional gateway issue. check BGP neighbors and route tables.
Evan: if LB health checks are failing we should do a controlled traffic shift. Priya, can you validate our traffic-shift runbook for sfo1->nyc2?
Priya: yes. runbook step 1: mark sfo1 pool unhealthy on global LB, step 2: kick gradual reroute with 10% steps, monitor 5xx and latency, rollback on >3% error delta.
Jorge: I'm getting `gcloud compute ssh` timeouts to all sfo1 jump hosts. control plane API is unreachable too — think we can't run k8s commands.
Evan: if we can't access control plane, rely on LB layer and region routing. Marta, can you confirm capacity available in nyc2 and sea1 for GPU workloads?
Marta: nyc2 has ~30% headroom across dedicated pools; sea1 ~15%. but spinning up extra dedicated capacity will trigger quota checks and preemptible fallback for some burst workloads. cost delta ~+30% if we fully shift.
Support-Shift: drafted comms: "We are investigating a regional networking outage affecting SFO. Customers on SFO may experience errors or degraded latency. We are shifting traffic and will post updates every 15m." Review?
Evan: good. Jorge, ask cloud provider for SR and network engineers. escalate if not responded in 5m.
Jorge: provider ACKed the SR, they're investigating edge gateway fabric. said they saw a partial control-plane isolation event. ETA unclear.
Priya: starting traffic shift now: marking sfo1 pool unhealthy -> kicking global LB reroute at 02:09 UTC. doing 10% step. monitoring.
SRE-Bot: action log: health_check_override applied to pool sfo1 at 1949994550 by Priya.
Evan: monitoring metrics during shift: initial 10% step shows error rate stable for hosted routes, dedicated customers with sticky sessions see brief reconnects.
Marta: starting warm-up for additional GPU nodes in nyc2 to absorb batch workloads. starting provisioning with `dedicated-provision --region nyc2 --count 8`.
Priya: at 50% shift now. latency on some routes increased +40ms but error rate within threshold. continuing.
Support-Shift: posting update to status page: "Traffic being shifted from SFO, mitigation in progress. No customer data exposure."
Jorge: provider responded: fabric issue at one of the regional edge routers, they have a mitigation rolling. could be 20-40m to clear.
Evan: finalizing incident lead: Priya you're IC. Marta you own capacity and cost tradeoffs. Jorge keep provider comms. Support-Shift keep customer updates every 15.
Priya: acknowledged. will keep increments here and move to incident bridge. creating IRC/bridge link now.
SRE-Bot: Incident INC-20260318-87 created and linked to this thread.
Evan: summary for execs: region sfo1 network isolation causing full edge-gateway loss; traffic being rerouted to nyc2/sea1, provisioning extra capacity; monitoring for cost and latency. next update in 10m. :thumbsup:
